topicName: Optimistic Rollups: Fraud Proofs, Challenge Periods, and Sequencing
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Optimistic Rollups: Fraud Proofs, Challenge Periods, and Sequencing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Optimistic Rollups are Layer 2 scaling solutions designed to increase Ethereum throughput while inheriting its security guarantees. They are termed \"optimistic\" because they assume transactions are valid by default and only run computation via fraud proofs when a challenge is raised."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Sequencers in Optimistic Rollups"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sequencers are specialized nodes responsible for ordering, bundling, and submitting transactions to the Layer 1 (Ethereum) smart contract. They provide instant transaction confirmation and state updates to users."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Centralized vs Decentralized Sequencing: Most current implementations use a single sequencer run by the rollup team, with roadmaps pointing toward decentralized sequencer sets."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MEV Extraction: Sequencers have the power to order transactions, opening avenues for Maximal Extractable Value (MEV)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Challenge Periods"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a sequencer posts a new state root to Layer 1, it enters a withdrawal or challenge period (typically lasting 7 days). During this time window, anyone can inspect the transaction data published on L1 and challenge the state root if it is incorrect."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Fraud Proof Mechanics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"If an invalid state transition is detected during the challenge period, a validator submits a fraud proof to the L1 rollup contract. The L1 contract executes the disputed transaction using the pre-state root to verify the correct post-state."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"function assertValidStateTransition(bytes32 preStateRoot, bytes calldata transactionData, bytes calldata proof) external { require(!executeAndVerify(preStateRoot, transactionData, proof), \"Fraud detected\"); }"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"If the fraud proof is successful, the invalid state root and all subsequent dependent batches are rolled back, and the malicious sequencer's bond is slashed."}]
